title: PDE STEELS Hub (SAS)
description: Pennsylvania's official one-stop hub for STEELS implementation: the standards, Foundation Boxes, curriculum frameworks, instructional resources, assessment guidance, safety guidelines, and recorded PDE webinars.
keywords: standards; foundation boxes; implementation; official; PDE
notes: THE authoritative starting point. Every STEELS question starts here. Verified via direct fetch.

title: STEELS Foundation Boxes & Webinar
description: PDE's standard-by-standard unpacking: each STEELS standard's supporting Foundation Box details the practices, core ideas, crosscutting concepts, PA contexts, and career-ready skills behind it, with a recorded walkthrough webinar by PDE Science Advisor David Bauman.
keywords: foundation boxes; unpacking; webinar; 3-dimensional
notes: Access via the STEELS Hub navigation (Standards section). The single best answer to 'what does this standard actually ask for?'

title: STEELS Curriculum Frameworks
description: PDE-developed frameworks for Science, Technology & Engineering, and Environmental Literacy & Sustainability that guide standards-based curriculum design, including big ideas, concepts, and competencies by grade level.
keywords: curriculum framework; scope and sequence; curriculum design
notes: Access via STEELS Hub navigation. Pair with district scope-and-sequence work.

title: STEELS Assessment Toolkit
description: PDE's three-module toolkit with ready-to-use three-dimensional performance tasks (e.g., Hurricane Boardwalk, Sea Stars, Snow Day), multidimensional rubrics, scoring guides, and facilitation guides for building local assessment literacy.
sciencePractices: Developing and Using Models; Constructing Explanations; Engaging in Argument from Evidence
keywords: performance tasks; rubrics; 3D assessment; PSSA; Keystone
notes: Access via STEELS Hub Assessment section. The only STEELS-explicit performance-task bank in existence. Unusually valuable and free.

title: STEELS Safety Guide
description: PDE's reference for safe classroom, laboratory, and field experiences under STEELS, with an introduction video and PowerPoint for staff training.
keywords: safety; lab safety; field experiences; liability
notes: Access via STEELS Hub. Administrators: this is your walkthrough/liability companion for hands-on science.

title: PDE Science Standards Page
description: The Commonwealth's official science standards page: the STEELS adoption timeline, sunset of the 2002 standards (June 30, 2025), full implementation expectations for 2025-26, and links to the STEELS Hub.
keywords: policy; timeline; implementation; compliance
notes: The citable source for board presentations and compliance questions. Verified via direct search.

title: SAS Portal (Standards Aligned System)
description: Pennsylvania's comprehensive standards portal: browse all PA standards including STEELS by grade and code, with linked materials, resources, and assessment information.
keywords: standards browser; SAS; alignment; standards codes
notes: Free account optional for saving materials. The standards-code browser behind future search-by-standard features.

title: Pennsylvania Gateway to Green
description: Statewide portal for PA environmental education: MWEE guidance, provider directory, grants (including PA DEP Environmental Education Grants), and professional learning across agencies and nonprofits.
publisher: PA Association of Environmental Educators & partners
keywords: MWEE; environmental education; grants; watershed; provider directory
notes: The connective tissue of PA environmental education — use it to find funding and partners for 3.4 work.

title: DCNR Watershed Education Program
description: Bureau of State Parks' interdisciplinary grades 6-12 watershed curriculum blending classroom and field investigation. DCNR explicitly states the curriculum supports the STEELS standards and the MWEE framework. Curriculum is obtained by attending a 1-2 day teacher workshop (Act 48 approved).
publisher: PA Department of Conservation and Natural Resources
disciplinaryCoreIdeas: ESS3: Earth and Human Activity; Environmental Literacy Skills; Sustainability and Stewardship
sciencePractices: Planning and Carrying Out Investigations; Analyzing and Interpreting Data
crosscuttingConcepts: Systems and System Models; Cause and Effect
keywords: watershed; field investigation; MWEE; Act 48; state parks; stream study
notes: EXPLICIT STEELS alignment stated by DCNR — rare and valuable. Includes on-loan water testing equipment and a statewide student data-sharing database. Verified 2026-07-24.

title: PA State Parks Educator Professional Development
description: DCNR's professional development menu for classroom and non-formal educators: Watershed Education workshops, Project Learning Tree, PA Songbirds (K-8), GO Teach, and more — all addressing PA academic standards including STEELS.
publisher: PA Department of Conservation and Natural Resources
keywords: Act 48; workshops; state parks; Project Learning Tree; outdoor learning
notes: Sign up for the State Parks monthly educator email to catch workshop announcements. Verified 2026-07-24.

title: Pennsylvania Envirothon
description: Statewide competition for teams of five high school students in aquatic ecology, forestry, soils, wildlife, and current environmental issues — combining classroom learning with outdoor field testing, run county-by-county through conservation districts.
disciplinaryCoreIdeas: LS2: Ecosystems; ESS3: Earth and Human Activity; Environmental Literacy Skills
sciencePractices: Analyzing and Interpreting Data; Engaging in Argument from Evidence
keywords: competition; Envirothon; field science; conservation; aquatics; forestry; soils; wildlife
notes: Study guides and resources on site; free PSECU-sponsored study app available. IU29's county competition runs through the Schuylkill Conservation District. Verified 2026-07-24.

title: PFBC Activities & Education Portal
description: Pennsylvania Fish & Boat Commission's free online portal: 100+ printable activity sheets, videos, publications, and newsletters on PA aquatic species, habitats, fishing, and water safety — all downloadable PDFs, no account needed.
disciplinaryCoreIdeas: LS1: Structures and Processes; LS2: Ecosystems
keywords: aquatic; fish; printable; activity sheets; Trout in the Classroom; no login
notes: Genuine Monday-morning material: print and go. Teachers page also connects to Trout in the Classroom and Watersheds programs. Verified 2026-07-24.

title: Schuylkill Conservation District Environmental Education
description: IU29's home-county partner for environmental education: school programs from 'Tickly & Prickly' (early learners) to 'Ways of Wildlife,' nature faires, summer day camps, and teacher workshops run in cooperation with Schuylkill Intermediate Unit 29.
keywords: Schuylkill County; local; field trips; teacher workshops; nature center; conservation district
notes: THE local anchor. Their own page cites the IU29 partnership — programs offered on a donation basis, including for special education populations. Verified 2026-07-24.

title: Stroud Water Research Center Curricula (WATERS, Shared Waters & more)
description: Free watershed science curricula from a world-class PA freshwater research center: the 10-lesson WATERS unit (middle school, UDL-designed, NSF-funded), Shared Waters (grades 3-6, NOAA-funded, emphasizing environmental literacy and sustainability), Trout Grow on Trees, and high school wetlands units.
disciplinaryCoreIdeas: LS2: Ecosystems; ESS2: Earth's Systems; Environmental Literacy Skills; Sustainability and Stewardship
sciencePractices: Planning and Carrying Out Investigations; Analyzing and Interpreting Data; Using Mathematics and Computational Thinking
crosscuttingConcepts: Systems and System Models; Stability and Change
keywords: watershed; MWEE; UDL; place-based; water quality; stream ecology; free curriculum
notes: Publisher states Shared Waters emphasizes environmental literacy and sustainability standards. WATERS uses Universal Design for Learning — a natural Living IEP Lab crossover. Free teacher account unlocks the learning portal. Verified 2026-07-24.

title: WikiWatershed / Model My Watershed
description: Stroud's free web toolkit for real watershed analysis: Model My Watershed lets students delineate any PA watershed, analyze land cover and soil data, and model runoff scenarios with actual geospatial data — professional-grade tools scaled for classrooms.
disciplinaryCoreIdeas: ESS2: Earth's Systems; ESS3: Earth and Human Activity
sciencePractices: Analyzing and Interpreting Data; Using Mathematics and Computational Thinking; Developing and Using Models
crosscuttingConcepts: Systems and System Models; Scale, Proportion, and Quantity
keywords: GIS; modeling; runoff; land use; real data; Schuylkill River; simulation
notes: Students can model their OWN school's watershed — instant place-based relevance for every IU29 district. Account optional for saving work.

title: Da Vinci Science Center STEELS Professional Development
description: Act 48-approved, STEELS-explicit professional development from PA's regional NGSX provider: Becoming a Next Generation Science Teacher courses, the PLANS pathway for administrators and instructional leaders, and traveling science programs with co-teaching support.
keywords: NGSX; Act 48; BNGST; PLANS; administrators; district contracts; Lehigh Valley
notes: Explicitly built for PA STEELS implementation; district-contracted pricing. The PLANS administrator pathway is one of very few PD offerings aimed at leaders rather than teachers. Verified 2026-07-24.

title: Hawk Mountain Sanctuary Education Programs
description: The world's first raptor sanctuary — on Schuylkill County's doorstep in Kempton — offering school programs, raptor migration data going back to 1934, and one of the region's most compelling natural phenomena for anchoring life science and data-analysis lessons.
keywords: raptors; migration; phenomena; field trip; long-term data; Kempton; local
notes: Program fees apply; migration count data is free online. The 90-year migration dataset is a ready-made local phenomenon for the Schuylkill Phenomena Bank. Program-page URL pending direct verification.

title: NASA STEM Learning Resources
description: NASA's searchable hub of free K-12 lessons, activities, and multimedia across Earth and space science, engineering design, and technology — filterable by grade and topic.
disciplinaryCoreIdeas: ESS1: Earth's Place in the Universe; ETS1: Engineering Design
keywords: space; Earth science; engineering; NASA; free lessons
notes: NASA reorganized its STEM pages recently — URL reflects the current hub; re-verify at quarterly link check.

title: NOAA Data in the Classroom
description: Structured modules where students use real NOAA environmental data — water quality, coral bleaching, ocean acidification — through scaffolded levels from guided exploration to independent investigation.
sciencePractices: Analyzing and Interpreting Data; Using Mathematics and Computational Thinking
keywords: real data; ocean; climate; water quality; modules
notes: FLAG: some modules (heat islands, El Niño, sea level) temporarily offline after a site migration and being restored. Check module availability before assigning; re-verify in October 2026.

title: NOAA Education Resource Collections
description: NOAA's curated collections of teaching resources on weather, climate, oceans, coasts, and watersheds — background science, multimedia, data, and lesson links organized by topic.
keywords: weather; climate; ocean; watersheds; collections
notes: More stable than Data in the Classroom during the migration; good background-building for teachers new to Earth systems content.

title: USGS Water Science School
description: The definitive free reference on all things water: the water cycle (including the updated diagram with human activity), groundwater, streamflow, water quality, and PA-relevant data — with diagrams, interactives, and real-time data links.
crosscuttingConcepts: Systems and System Models; Energy and Matter
keywords: water cycle; groundwater; streams; real-time data; no login
notes: Pairs perfectly with local watershed work — USGS real-time gauges exist on the Schuylkill and Swatara. No account, no ads, no fuss.

title: EPA Students & Educators Resources
description: EPA's free environmental education materials: lesson plans and project ideas on air, water, waste, and climate, plus environmental data tools students can use for local investigations.
keywords: environment; air quality; waste; climate; EPA
notes: Useful for the human-impact side of 3.4; quality varies by page, so preview before assigning.

title: Smithsonian Science for Makerspaces
description: Nine free engineering design challenges for grades 1-5 connecting emerging technologies to hands-on making — each with teacher guides, material lists, and explicit engineering-design framing from the Smithsonian Science Education Center.
sciencePractices: Designing Solutions; Planning and Carrying Out Investigations
keywords: makerspace; engineering design; elementary; hands-on; free challenges
notes: Directly bridges Make @ Skook29 makerspace programming with elementary 3.5 standards. Exact URL pending direct verification (confirmed via Smithsonian press release).

title: GLOBE Program
description: NASA/NOAA-sponsored international program where students collect real environmental data (atmosphere, hydrosphere, biosphere, soil) using vetted protocols and contribute to a global scientific database.
sciencePractices: Planning and Carrying Out Investigations; Analyzing and Interpreting Data
keywords: citizen science; protocols; data collection; global database; field work
notes: Teacher training required for data entry (free, online). Turns any schoolyard into a research station.

title: NextGenScience (nextgenscience.org)
description: The home of the Next Generation Science Standards — the national standards STEELS was adapted from — including the standards browser, evidence statements, and implementation resources.
keywords: NGSS; evidence statements; standards; national
notes: Because STEELS is NGSS-adapted, nearly everything here transfers — but always check against PA Foundation Boxes, especially for 3.4 and 3.5, which differ.

title: Examples of Quality NGSS Design (incl. EQuIP Rubric)
description: Vetted example units and lessons that earned the NGSS Design Badge, plus the EQuIP Rubric for evaluating whether instructional materials are genuinely three-dimensional — the screening tool PA's own STEELS 101 guidance points teachers toward.
keywords: EQuIP; curriculum screening; quality examples; design badge; vetting
notes: Cited in PDE's STEELS 101 document. The tool for answering 'is this curriculum we're being sold actually 3-D?'

title: STEM Teaching Tools
description: Short, research-based practice briefs from the University of Washington on every aspect of 3-D science teaching: talk moves, assessment, equity, phenomena selection, and family engagement — each a focused 2-page read built for PLCs.
publisher: University of Washington Institute for Science + Math Education
keywords: practice briefs; PLC; equity; talk moves; phenomena; research-based
notes: Cited in PDE's STEELS 101 guidance. The best PLC fuel in science education — pick one brief per meeting and go.

title: OpenSciEd
description: Complete, free, openly licensed NGSS science units for elementary, middle, and high school — storyline-driven, phenomenon-anchored, and externally reviewed, with teacher guides, slides, and student materials.
keywords: full curriculum; storylines; phenomena; OER; free units; field-tested
notes: Free account required to download. The strongest free full-curriculum option for districts that can't buy new materials — pair adoption with PD, not as a PDF dump.

title: The Wonder of Science
description: Paul Andersen's practical 3-D teaching site: phenomena organized by standard and grade, Claim-Evidence-Reasoning templates and rubrics, assessment probes, and clear explainer videos for every SEP and CCC.
keywords: phenomena; CER; claim evidence reasoning; rubrics; videos; by standard
notes: Probably the fastest on-ramp for a teacher who's never taught 3-D. Phenomena indexed by performance expectation — map to STEELS via the NGSS crosswalk.

title: Ambitious Science Teaching
description: A coherent framework of core teaching practices — planning for engagement, eliciting student ideas, supporting sensemaking, and pressing for evidence-based explanations — with free tools, videos of real classrooms, and discourse primers.
keywords: core practices; discourse; sensemaking; classroom videos; framework
estimatedTime: Tool-based; book study over a semester
notes: The pedagogical backbone behind programs like NGSX. Classroom video library is gold for coaching conversations.

title: A Framework for K-12 Science Education
description: The National Academies consensus report that STEELS (via NGSS) is built on — the definitive explanation of the three dimensions, why they matter, and how learning progresses K-12. Free PDF download.
keywords: framework; research basis; three dimensions; National Research Council
notes: Free PDF (email requested at download). PDE cites this as a primary source document for STEELS. When someone asks 'why are we changing how we teach science?' — this is the answer, with receipts.

title: Stanford NGSS Assessment Project (SNAP)
description: Free three-dimensional performance assessments from Stanford SCALE: short performance assessments, instructionally-embedded tasks, multidimensional rubric templates, and free online courses teaching educators to design their own — including rare K-4 examples.
sciencePractices: Developing and Using Models; Constructing Explanations; Engaging in Argument from Evidence
keywords: performance assessment; rubrics; 3D assessment; task design; free courses
notes: The natural companion to PDE's Assessment Toolkit — use SNAP's design tools to build IU29-original tasks. Verified 2026-07-24.

title: PhET Interactive Simulations
description: 170+ free, research-based science and math simulations from CU Boulder — forces, circuits, states of matter, natural selection, and more — running in-browser with no account, plus teacher-contributed lesson plans.
disciplinaryCoreIdeas: PS1: Matter; PS2: Motion and Stability; PS3: Energy; LS4: Evolution
sciencePractices: Developing and Using Models; Planning and Carrying Out Investigations
keywords: simulations; physics; chemistry; no login; interactive; inquiry
notes: The gold standard for no-friction interactive science. Works on Chromebooks, no accounts, translated into dozens of languages.

title: Concord Consortium STEM Resource Finder
description: Free, technology-rich science activities and virtual labs — molecular dynamics, genetics, seismic data, sensor-based investigations — with class-management features for tracking student work.
keywords: virtual labs; molecular; genetics; sensors; models
notes: Free accounts unlock assignment tracking. Concord co-developed Stroud's WATERS curriculum — same design DNA.

title: CODAP (Common Online Data Analysis Platform)
description: Free, browser-based data analysis built for education: drag-and-drop graphing, mapping, and modeling of any dataset — the easiest serious on-ramp to data science practices in 6-12 science.
sciencePractices: Analyzing and Interpreting Data; Using Mathematics and Computational Thinking
keywords: data analysis; data science; graphing; computational thinking; no login
notes: Drop in local data — Envirothon results, stream monitoring, Hawk Mountain counts — and 'CT is the OS' becomes a lesson, not a slogan.

title: TeachEngineering
description: The largest free K-12 engineering library: 1,650+ NSF-funded, teacher-tested lessons and hands-on activities from 50+ university engineering programs, searchable by grade, cost of materials, and time — no account required.
disciplinaryCoreIdeas: ETS1: Engineering Design; ETS2: Links Among Engineering, Technology, Science, and Society
sciencePractices: Designing Solutions; Asking Questions and Defining Problems
keywords: engineering; design challenges; hands-on; NSF; no login; maker
notes: The backbone for 3.5 — a domain where PA teachers have the least prior training. Filter by low-cost materials for makerspace-on-a-budget builds.

title: National Science Teaching Association (NSTA)
description: The national professional association for science educators: free Daily Do sensemaking lessons, journals, position statements, web seminars, and an extensive resource library — with deeper access via paid membership.
keywords: professional association; Daily Do; journals; web seminars; membership
notes: Free account unlocks a meaningful slice; full journals and books require paid membership (~$89/yr individual). Clearly disclose the tier when recommending.

title: PBLWorks
description: The Buck Institute's gold-standard project-based learning resources: the research-based Gold Standard PBL model, a searchable project idea library, rubrics, and planning tools.
keywords: PBL; gold standard; project library; rubrics; driving questions
notes: Free account for the project library; paid PD services. Use the Gold Standard design elements as the quality bar for IU29-original design challenges.

title: Project Learning Tree
description: Award-winning environmental education using forests as a lens: the Explore Your Environment K-8 guide contains 50 field-tested activities; in PA, workshops and materials are delivered through DCNR as the state host.
keywords: forests; trees; outdoor learning; activity guide; workshops
notes: K-8 guide is $34.99 print or obtained via workshop (often through DCNR PA workshops, sometimes included in registration). Some free sample activities online. Access clearly disclosed: primarily paid/workshop.

title: Exploratorium Tinkering Studio & Science Snacks
description: The Exploratorium's free maker-education activities and 'Science Snacks' — cheap-materials versions of museum exhibits with clear science explanations — from the institution that basically invented museum-based tinkering pedagogy.
keywords: tinkering; maker; science snacks; cheap materials; exhibits
notes: Science Snacks are ideal makerspace stations. URL pending direct verification at quarterly link check.

title: PBS LearningMedia
description: Free standards-searchable library of videos, interactives, and lesson plans from PBS and partner producers (NOVA, Nature, local stations including WVIA/WITF), organized by grade and subject.
keywords: video; NOVA; media; interactives; free account optional
notes: Optional free account for saving. Search by standard is NGSS-based — crosswalk to STEELS applies.

title: Mystery Science
description: Highly popular ready-made elementary science lessons built around mystery phenomena, with videos, discussion prompts, and simple-materials hands-on activities — a lifeline for elementary generalists.
keywords: elementary; phenomena; ready-made; videos; hands-on
notes: Limited free lessons; full access requires school/district subscription. Included despite paid status because elementary demand is intense and quality is real — clearly labeled as paid.

title: HHMI BioInteractive
description: Free, stunning high school life science resources: data-rich case studies, short films, interactive media, and click-and-learn activities on evolution, ecology, and molecular biology — built by scientists, beloved by AP and honors teachers.
disciplinaryCoreIdeas: LS1: Structures and Processes; LS2: Ecosystems; LS4: Biological Evolution
sciencePractices: Analyzing and Interpreting Data; Constructing Explanations
keywords: biology; evolution; case studies; short films; data; high school
notes: Free account for full downloads. Directly strengthens the thin 9-12 life science band; strong Keystone Biology relevance.

title: NextGen Science Storylines
description: Free, coherent storyline units from Northwestern University where each lesson is driven by student questions about an anchoring phenomenon — the instructional model behind OpenSciEd, with units for elementary through high school.
keywords: storylines; anchoring phenomena; coherence; units; Northwestern
notes: URL pending direct verification at quarterly link check. Excellent for showing teachers what phenomenon-driven coherence looks like before committing to full OpenSciEd adoption.

title: Macroinvertebrates.org
description: Free interactive atlas for identifying aquatic insects of eastern North America with stunning zoomable photography — the digital field guide for stream studies, Leaf Pack investigations, and Envirothon aquatics prep.
publisher: Carnegie Mellon University & Stroud Water Research Center
keywords: macroinvertebrates; stream study; identification; aquatic insects; water quality; no login
notes: Cited by PA conservation districts as a core teaching resource. Load it on tablets for creek days — bioassessment becomes self-serve.

title: Code.org
description: Free K-12 computer science curriculum: CS Fundamentals for elementary, CS Discoveries for middle school, CS Principles for high school — with teacher dashboards, self-paced PD, and no-cost everything.
keywords: computer science; coding; CS Fundamentals; curriculum; free PD
notes: Free teacher accounts for class management. The default statewide CS on-ramp — connects to your CSO Regional Lead network.

title: CS Unplugged
description: Free computational thinking activities that teach CS concepts — algorithms, binary, sorting networks — entirely without computers, using cards, string, and movement. Perfect for K-8 and low-tech classrooms.
keywords: unplugged; computational thinking; no computers; algorithms; kinesthetic
notes: No devices, no accounts, no excuses. The cleanest demonstration that computational thinking is thinking, not typing.

title: Scratch
description: MIT's free block-based programming environment where students create interactive stories, games, and science simulations — the world's largest kids' coding community, with an educator dashboard for classes.
keywords: block coding; MIT; creative computing; simulations; projects
notes: Accounts optional (needed for saving/sharing). Have students BUILD science simulations rather than just use them — modeling practice meets computational thinking.

title: CSTA K-12 Computer Science Standards
description: The national K-12 computer science standards framework — the reference point for mapping computational thinking connections across STEELS domains and for districts building CS pathways.
keywords: CS standards; CSTA; framework; pathways; computational thinking
notes: Use alongside STEELS T&E standards when advising districts on integrated CS. URL pending direct verification.
